Why seed banks aren't the only answer to food security

This article addresses one side of the argument, but to be honest there is another side. I have advocated for ages for everyone to grow a garden. I don't care if it is a pot in a window sill. By demanding rare varieties we can save those varieties. It creates a commercial demand, which makes farmers of these varieties money, and keeps them alive. Additionally, if you have more space to grow you can save your own seed from unique varieties. I am heavily invested in gardening and homesteading in general, and part of drew me to it was the ability to have food I can not buy in the store. Where I live the selection is crap, so it was not poverty...it was literally not available at any price. (I moved south after being a spoiled foodie in the north east)

Gardening, saving seeds, and preserving the traditional dishes I love, through my own family has helped. If millions more did this, our world would have a very diverse seed stock. Plus it's so much fun to raise from a seed a little plant that my native ancestors ate daily two centuries ago.

A group collectively known as the Sea Peoples raised a bunch of hell along the coast of the Mediterranean and especially Egypt starting about 100 years before the accepted time of the Bronze Age collapse (c. 1177 BCE). These invasions were one cause of many; the Egyptians managed to hold their own during such battles but it was costly. In that same time frame various insurrections, wars between kingdoms, economic problems, and natural disasters all happened to be focused on a relatively small and previously well-developed part of the world. It's generally accepted that as an event, the end of the Late Bronze Age came about relatively quickly and violently. This should not be taken to mean that the process was by any means simple...numerous groups appeared and disappeared disrupting established culture; there was also a drought as well as a volcanic eruption (Hekla 3) that was so absurdly huge it is assumed to be responsible for dropping the temperature of the Northern Hemisphere for years.
